Only Statement I and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT3_Q04 - Electrolyte classification, limiting molar conductivity extrapolation, and weak acid dissociation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following three statements regarding electrolytic conductivity and Kohlrausch's law:

Statement I: In the Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation \(\Lambda_{\text{m}} = \Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - A c^{1/2}\), the constant \(A\) depends only on the dielectric properties of the solvent and is completely independent of the charges on the electrolyte ions.

Statement II: The limiting molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ\)) of weak electrolytes like acetic acid cannot be obtained by graphical extrapolation of \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}\) versus \(c^{1/2}\) because \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}\) increases sharply near zero concentration.

Statement III: For a weak monobasic electrolyte, the acid dissociation constant \(K_{\text{a}}\) can be expressed in terms of molar conductivities as \(K_{\text{a}} = \frac{c \Lambda_{\text{m}}^2}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ (\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - \Lambda_{\text{m}})}\).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

विद्युत-अपघटनी चालकता तथा कोलराउश नियम के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित तीन कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: डेबाई-हुकेल-ओनसेगर समीकरण \(\Lambda_{\text{m}} = \Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - A c^{1/2}\) में, स्थिरांक \(A\) केवल विलायक के परावैद्युत गुणों पर निर्भर करता है तथा यह विद्युत-अपघट्य के आयनों के आवेशों से पूर्णतः स्वतंत्र होता है।

कथन II: एसीटिक अम्ल जैसे दुर्बल विद्युत-अपघट्यों की सीमांत मोलर चालकता (\(\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ\)) को \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}\) तथा \(c^{1/2}\) के आलेख के बहिर्वेशन द्वारा प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता क्योंकि शून्य सांद्रता के निकट \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}\) में तीव्र वृद्धि होती है।

कथन III: किसी दुर्बल एक-क्षारकीय विद्युत-अपघट्य के लिए, अम्ल वियोजन स्थिरांक \(K_{\text{a}}\) को मोलर चालकताओं के पदों में \(K_{\text{a}} = \frac{c \Lambda_{\text{m}}^2}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ (\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - \Lambda_{\text{m}})}\) के रूप में व्यक्त किया जा सकता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the constant in the Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation
For strong electrolytes, the concentration dependence of molar conductivity is described by: \[ \Lambda_{\text{m}} = \Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - A c^{1/2} \] The parameter \(A\) accounts for electrophoretic and relaxation field effects that retard ion motion. According to electrolyte theory and NCERT principles, the value of the constant \(A\) for a given solvent and temperature depends fundamentally on the type of electrolyte, specifically the magnitude of electric charges on the cation and anion produced upon dissociation (for example, electrolytes are categorized into 1-1 like \(\text{NaCl}\), 2-1 like \(\text{CaCl}_2\), and 2-2 like \(\text{MgSO}_4\), each type possessing a distinct characteristic value for \(A\)). Therefore, asserting that \(A\) is completely independent of the ionic charges is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the extrapolation limitation for weak electrolytes
Weak electrolytes maintain a low degree of dissociation at finite concentrations. As dilution proceeds, Ostwald's dilution law dictates that the degree of dissociation (\(\alpha\)) increases dramatically as concentration approaches zero. Consequently, the plot of \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}\) versus \(c^{1/2}\) exhibits a steep, nearly asymptotic upward curve toward the y-axis at very low concentrations. Because the curve becomes virtually vertical and parallel to the \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}\) axis, graphical extrapolation to \(c = 0\) cannot yield a reliable intercept for \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ\). Hence, the second statement is scientifically valid.

Step 3: Derivation of the dissociation constant expression from molar conductivities
For a weak monobasic acid undergoing the equilibrium \(\text{HA} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{A}^-\), the degree of dissociation is given by \(\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}\). Substituting \(\alpha\) into Ostwald's dissociation constant equation: \[ K_{\text{a}} = \frac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha} = \frac{c \left(\frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}\right)^2}{1 - \frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}} = \frac{c \frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^2}{(\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ)^2}}{\frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - \Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}} = \frac{c \Lambda_{\text{m}}^2}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ (\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - \Lambda_{\text{m}})} \] This algebraic relation directly links the measured molar conductivities to the thermodynamic equilibrium constant. Hence, the third statement is scientifically valid.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The dependence of the Debye-Hückel constant on ionic charges is misrepresented in the first statement, whereas the extrapolation failure and dissociation constant expression are mathematically and physically correct. Therefore, only Statement II and Statement III are correct.

चरण 1: डेबाई-हुकेल-ओनसेगर समीकरण के स्थिरांक का मूल्यांकन
समीकरण \(\Lambda_{\text{m}} = \Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - A c^{1/2}\) में स्थिरांक \(A\) का मान दिए गए विलायक और ताप पर विद्युत-अपघट्य के प्रकार अर्थात धनायन और ऋणायन पर उपस्थित आवेशों (जैसे 1-1, 2-1, 2-2 आदि) पर निर्भर करता है। अतः यह दावा करना कि \(A\) आयनों के आवेश पर निर्भर नहीं करता, गलत है। अतः पहला कथन असत्य है।

चरण 2: दुर्बल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के बहिर्वेशन की सीमा का मूल्यांकन
एसीटिक अम्ल जैसे दुर्बल विद्युत-अपघट्यों के लिए तनुता बढ़ाने पर वियोजन की मात्रा अत्यधिक तेजी से बढ़ती है। शून्य सांद्रता के निकट आलेख इतना तीव्र हो जाता है कि यह अक्ष के लगभग समांतर हो जाता है, जिससे बहिर्वेशन द्वारा \(\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ\) ज्ञात नहीं किया जा सकता। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: वियोजन स्थिरांक के व्यंजक का मूल्यांकन
दुर्बल अम्ल के लिए वियोजन की मात्रा \(\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}\) होती है। इसे ओस्टवाल्ड के सूत्र में रखने पर: \[ K_{\text{a}} = \frac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha} = \frac{c \left(\frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}\right)^2}{1 - \frac{\Lambda_{\text{m}}}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ}} = \frac{c \Lambda_{\text{m}}^2}{\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ (\Lambda_{\text{m}}^\circ - \Lambda_{\text{m}})} \] यह व्यंजक गणितीय रूप से पूर्णतः सही है। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
पहला कथन असत्य है, जबकि दूसरा और तीसरा कथन सत्य हैं। अतः केवल कथन II और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Only Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statements I, II and III are all correct.
Only Statement I and Statement III are correct.
Only Statement II and Statement III are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT4_Q01 - Electrochemical mechanism and thermodynamics of atmospheric corrosion of iron

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the corrosion (rusting) of iron in the atmosphere:

Statement I: Rusting of iron is an electrochemical process where oxidation of iron to ferrous ions (\(\text{Fe}^{2+}\)) occurs at an anodic spot on the metal surface.

Statement II: Electrons released at the anodic spot travel through the metal to another spot which acts as a cathode to reduce atmospheric oxygen in the presence of \(\text{H}^+\) ions.

Statement III: The \(\text{H}^+\) ions essential for the reduction of oxygen at the cathodic spot are provided by carbonic acid formed from the dissolution of atmospheric \(\text{CO}_2\) in water.

Statement IV: The standard electrode potential for the iron oxidation half-reaction at the anode is \(E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = +0.44\text{ V}\).

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

वायुमंडल में लोहे के संक्षारण (जंग लगने) के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: लोहे पर जंग लगना एक वैद्युत-रासायनिक परिघटना है जहाँ धातु की सतह पर एक एनोडी स्थल पर लोहे का फेरस आयनों (\(\text{Fe}^{2+}\)) में ऑक्सीकरण होता है।

कथन II: एनोडी स्थल पर मुक्त हुए इलेक्ट्रॉन धातु के माध्यम से दूसरे स्थल पर पहुँचते हैं, जो कैथोड की भाँति कार्य करके \(\text{H}^+\) आयनों की उपस्थिति में वायुमंडलीय ऑक्सीजन का अपचयन करता है।

कथन III: कैथोडी स्थल पर ऑक्सीजन के अपचयन के लिए आवश्यक \(\text{H}^+\) आयन जल में वायुमंडलीय \(\text{CO}_2\) के घुलने से बनने वाले कार्बोनिक अम्ल द्वारा उपलब्ध होते हैं।

कथन IV: एनोड पर होने वाली लोहे की ऑक्सीकरण अर्ध-अभिक्रिया के लिए मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव \(E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = +0.44\text{ V}\) होता है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the anodic oxidation process in corrosion
Corrosion of iron is fundamentally an electrochemical process. At a specific strain site or defect on the iron surface, iron atoms lose electrons and undergo oxidation to enter the aqueous film as ferrous ions: \[ \text{Anode: } 2\text{Fe(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 4\text{e}^- \] This site behaves as the anode of a localized galvanic cell. Hence, the first statement is scientifically valid.

Step 2: Evaluation of electron conduction and cathodic reduction
The electrons released during the oxidation of iron migrate through the bulk metallic conductor to another region on the iron surface where dissolved oxygen is available. This region acts as a cathode, where molecular oxygen is reduced to water in an acidic aqueous environment: \[ \text{Cathode: } \text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 4\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \] The overall electrochemical cell reaction is: \[ 2\text{Fe(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 4\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \] Hence, the second statement is scientifically valid.

Step 3: Evaluation of the source of hydrogen ions
The cathodic reduction of oxygen requires hydrogen ions (\(\text{H}^+\Default\)). In atmospheric corrosion, these ions are primarily generated when atmospheric carbon dioxide dissolves in the surface water film to form weakly dissociated carbonic acid: \[ \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{CO}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+ + \text{HCO}_3^- \] Additional \(\text{H}^+\) ions can arise from dissolved acidic air pollutants like sulfur dioxide. Hence, the third statement is scientifically valid.

Step 4: Evaluation of the standard electrode potential of the iron couple
According to IUPAC convention, standard electrode potentials are defined as reduction potentials. For the \(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}\) redox couple: \[ \text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Fe(s)}, \quad E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = -0.44\text{ V} \] The value is \(-0.44\text{ V}\), reflecting that metallic iron is thermodynamically susceptible to oxidation relative to standard hydrogen. The claim that \(E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})}\) is \(+0.44\text{ V}\) incorrectly asserts a positive reduction potential. Hence, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first, second, and third statements accurately state the electrochemical mechanism, while the fourth statement gives an erroneous sign for the standard electrode potential. Therefore, only Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.

चरण 1: संक्षारण में एनोडी ऑक्सीकरण प्रक्रम का मूल्यांकन
लोहे पर जंग लगना एक वैद्युत-रासायनिक प्रक्रम है। लोहे की वस्तु के किसी विशिष्ट स्थल पर ऑक्सीकरण होता है और वह स्थल एनोड की भाँति व्यवहार करता है: \[ \text{एनोड: } 2\text{Fe(s)} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 4\text{e}^- \] अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: इलेक्ट्रॉन अभिगमन तथा कैथोडी अपचयन का मूल्यांकन
एनोडी स्थल पर मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन धातु के माध्यम से दूसरे स्थल पर जाते हैं तथा \(\text{H}^+\) आयनों की उपस्थिति में ऑक्सीजन का अपचयन करते हैं: \[ \text{कैथोड: } \text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 4\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \] समग्र अभिक्रिया \(2\text{Fe(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 4\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}\) होती है। अतः दूसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 3: हाइड्रोजन आयनों के स्रोत का मूल्यांकन
ऑक्सीजन के अपचयन के लिए आवश्यक \(\text{H}^+\) आयन जल में वायुमंडलीय \(\text{CO}_2\) के घुलने से बनने वाले कार्बोनिक अम्ल (\(\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\)) के वियोजन से प्राप्त होते हैं। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: आयरन युग्म के मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव का मूल्यांकन
IUPAC परिपाटी के अनुसार, मानक इलेक्ट्रोड विभव अपचयन विभव के रूप में व्यक्त किए जाते हैं। \(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}\) अर्ध-सेल के लिए मानक अपचयन विभव \(E^\circ_{(\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe})} = -0.44\text{ V}\) होता है। कथन में दिया गया मान \(+0.44\text{ V}\) गलत है। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I, II और III सत्य हैं जबकि कथन IV असत्य है। अतः केवल कथन I, कथन II और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Only Statement I and Statement IV are correct.
Only Statement I, Statement II and Statement III are correct.
Only Statement II and Statement IV are correct.
Statements I, II, III and IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CLASS12_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT4_Q02 - Faraday laws, electrolytic stoichiometry, and concentration effects on products

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the quantitative aspects and products of electrolysis:

Statement I: The reduction of one mole of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) ions to aluminium metal requires exactly \(3\text{ F}\) of electricity, which corresponds to approximately \(2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C}\) of charge.

Statement II: According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis, the amount of chemical reaction occurring at any electrode is inversely proportional to the quantity of electricity passed through the electrolyte.

Statement III: During the electrolysis of sulfuric acid, oxygen gas is predominantly liberated at the anode when the acid is dilute, whereas peroxodisulphate ions (\(\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\)) are preferentially formed at higher sulfuric acid concentrations.

Statement IV: In the industrial electrolytic refining of copper, pure copper is made the anode which dissolves into solution, while impure copper forms the cathode where refined metal deposits.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

विद्युत-अपघटन के मात्रात्मक पहलुओं तथा उत्पादों के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित चार कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

कथन I: \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) आयनों के 1 मोल को ऐलुमिनियम धातु में अपचयित करने के लिए ठीक \(3\text{ F}\) विद्युत की आवश्यकता होती है, जो लगभग \(2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C}\) आवेश के संगत है।

कथन II: फैराडे के विद्युत-अपघटन के प्रथम नियम के अनुसार, किसी इलेक्ट्रोड पर होने वाली रासायनिक अभिक्रिया की मात्रा विद्युत-अपघट्य में प्रवाहित विद्युत की मात्रा के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

कथन III: सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के विद्युत-अपघटन के दौरान, तनु अम्ल होने पर एनोड पर मुख्य रूप से ऑक्सीजन गैस मुक्त होती है, जबकि सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल की उच्च सांद्रता पर प्राथमिकता से परऑक्सोडाइसल्फेट आयन (\(\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\)) बनते हैं।

कथन IV: कॉपर के औद्योगिक विद्युत-अपघटनी शोधन में, शुद्ध कॉपर को एनोड बनाया जाता है जो विलयन में घुलता है, जबकि अशुद्ध कॉपर कैथोड बनाता है जिस पर शोधित धातु निक्षेपित होती है।

नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर का चयन कीजिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the stoichiometric charge for aluminium reduction
The reduction half-reaction for aluminium is: \[ \text{Al}^{3+}\text{(l)} + 3\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Al(s)} \] The reduction of one mole of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) requires \(3\text{ moles of electrons}\), corresponding to \(3\text{ Faraday}\) (\(3\text{ F}\)) of electricity. Using the Faraday constant \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\): \[ Q = 3 \times 96487\text{ C} = 289461\text{ C} \approx 2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C} \] Hence, the first statement is scientifically valid.

Step 2: Evaluation of Faraday's first law of electrolysis
Faraday's first law states that the mass of a substance liberated or deposited at any electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electric charge passed through the electrolyte: \[ m \propto Q \implies m = z \cdot Q = z \cdot I \cdot t \] The statement erroneously claims an inverse proportionality. Hence, the second statement is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the anodic oxidation of sulfuric acid
During the electrolysis of sulfuric acid, two competing oxidation processes can occur at the anode: \[ 2\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{O}_2\text{(g)} + 4\text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + 4\text{e}^-, \quad E^\circ = +1.23\text{ V} \] \[ 2\text{SO}_4^{2-}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^-, \quad E^\circ = +1.96\text{ V} \] For dilute sulfuric acid, water oxidation to \(\text{O}_2\) is favored. However, at higher concentrations of \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), where sulfate ions are abundant and water activity is reduced, the oxidation of sulfate ions to peroxodisulphate (\(\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\)) becomes predominant. Hence, the third statement is scientifically valid.

Step 4: Evaluation of the electrode configuration in electrolytic copper refining
In the industrial refining of blister copper, the impure copper block is connected as the anode, which undergoes oxidation and dissolves into the \(\text{CuSO}_4\) electrolyte: \[ \text{Anode (oxidation): } \text{Cu(impure)} \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^- \] A thin strip of highly pure copper serves as the cathode, upon which copper ions from the solution deposit as refined metal: \[ \text{Cathode (reduction): } \text{Cu}^{2+}\text{(aq)} + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Cu(pure)} \] The statement reverses these assignments by asserting that pure copper acts as the dissolving anode and impure copper acts as the cathode. Hence, the fourth statement is incorrect.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
The first and third statements are scientifically valid, whereas the second and fourth statements contain factual inaccuracies. Therefore, only Statement I and Statement III are correct.

चरण 1: ऐलुमिनियम अपचयन के रससमीकरणमितीय आवेश का मूल्यांकन
अर्ध-अभिक्रिया \(\text{Al}^{3+} + 3\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Al}\) के अनुसार, 1 मोल \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) के अपचयन हेतु 3 मोल इलेक्ट्रॉनों अर्थात \(3\text{ F}\) विद्युत की आवश्यकता होती है: \[ Q = 3 \times 96487\text{ C} = 289461\text{ C} \approx 2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C} \] अतः पहला कथन सत्य है।

चरण 2: फैराडे के प्रथम नियम का मूल्यांकन
फैराडे के प्रथम नियम के अनुसार, किसी इलेक्ट्रोड पर निक्षेपित पदार्थ की मात्रा प्रवाहित विद्युत आवेश के समानुपाती (\(m \propto Q\)) होती है, व्युत्क्रमानुपाती नहीं। अतः दूसरा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 3: सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के एनोडी ऑक्सीकरण का मूल्यांकन
तनु सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल के विद्युत-अपघटन में एनोड पर जल का ऑक्सीकरण होकर \(\text{O}_2\) गैस मुक्त होती है, जबकि सल्फ्यूरिक अम्ल की उच्च सांद्रता पर सल्फेट आयन ऑक्सीकृत होकर परऑक्सोडाइसल्फेट (\(\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\)) बनाते हैं। अतः तीसरा कथन सत्य है।

चरण 4: कॉपर के विद्युत-अपघटनी शोधन के इलेक्ट्रोडों का मूल्यांकन
कॉपर के शोधन में अशुद्ध कॉपर को एनोड बनाया जाता है जो घुलता है, तथा शुद्ध कॉपर की पतली पट्टी को कैथोड बनाया जाता है जिस पर शुद्ध धातु निक्षेपित होती है। कथन में यह क्रम उल्टा दिया गया है। अतः चौथा कथन असत्य है।

चरण 5: अंतिम निष्कर्ष
कथन I और III सत्य हैं, जबकि कथन II और IV असत्य हैं। अतः केवल कथन I और कथन III सही हैं।

answer.text: Only Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Only Statement II and Statement IV are correct.
Only Statement I and Statement III are correct.
Only Statement III and Statement IV are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q01 - Match physical quantities with their SI units

questiontext.text:
Match the electrochemical quantities in List I with their corresponding SI units in List II:

List IList II
A. Resistance (\(R\))I. \(\text{S m}^{-1}\)
B. Resistivity (\(\rho\))II. \(\Omega\text{ m}\)
C. Conductivity (\(\kappa\))III. \(\text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)
D. Molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m\))IV. \(\Omega\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Definitions
The quantities under consideration are electrical resistance (\(R\)), resistivity (\(\rho\)), conductivity (\(\kappa\)), and molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m\)).

Step 2: Physical Formulas and Unit Derivations
Resistance is expressed as \(R = \rho \frac{l}{A}\), and its SI unit is ohm (\(\Omega\)).
Resistivity is defined by \(\rho = \frac{R A}{l}\), yielding the SI unit \(\Omega \times \frac{\text{m}^2}{\text{m}} = \Omega\text{ m}\).
Conductivity represents the reciprocal of resistivity, \(\kappa = \frac{1}{\rho}\), giving the SI unit \(\Omega^{-1}\text{ m}^{-1} = \text{S m}^{-1}\).
Molar conductivity is defined by \(\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa}{c}\), where \(\kappa\) is in \(\text{S m}^{-1}\) and concentration \(c\) is in \(\text{mol m}^{-3}\), resulting in the SI unit \(\frac{\text{S m}^{-1}}{\text{mol m}^{-3}} = \text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Resistance corresponds to \(\Omega\).
Resistivity corresponds to \(\Omega\text{ m}\).
Conductivity corresponds to \(\text{S m}^{-1}\).
Molar conductivity corresponds to \(\text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
The derived units fully conform to SI base and derived quantity definitions.
Final Conceptual Answer: Resistance pairs with \(\Omega\), resistivity pairs with \(\Omega\text{ m}\), conductivity pairs with \(\text{S m}^{-1}\), and molar conductivity pairs with \(\text{S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q02 - Match commercial batteries with their characteristics

questiontext.text:
Match the electrochemical cells/batteries in List I with their characteristic features in List II:

List IList II
A. Dry cell (Leclanché cell)I. Uses zinc-mercury amalgam and maintains a constant voltage of about \(1.35\text{ V}\)
B. Mercury cellII. Secondary cell containing lead dioxide cathode and \(38\%\) sulphuric acid
C. Lead storage batteryIII. Directly converts heat of combustion of gaseous fuels into electricity with about \(70\%\) efficiency
D. Fuel cellIV. Primary cell with a zinc container anode and carbon cathode giving about \(1.5\text{ V}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principles of Battery Types
Primary cells cannot be recharged because the redox reaction occurs only once. Secondary batteries are rechargeable through the application of an external reverse current. Fuel cells continuously convert fuel combustion free energy into electrical energy.

Step 2: Detailed Evaluation of Each Cell
The dry cell (Leclanché cell) employs a zinc container anode and a carbon rod cathode surrounded by powdered \(\text{MnO}_2\) and carbon, furnishing a potential of approximately \(1.5\text{ V}\).
The mercury cell features a \(\text{Zn(Hg)}\) amalgam anode and a paste of \(\text{HgO}\) and carbon cathode, delivering a stable potential of nearly \(1.35\text{ V}\) throughout its operational lifetime because no ions in solution undergo net concentration change.
The lead storage battery is a secondary cell consisting of a spongy lead anode, a \(\text{PbO}_2\)-packed lead grid cathode, and \(38\%\) \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) electrolyte solution.
The \(\text{H}_2\text{--O}_2\) fuel cell directly transforms the combustion energy of hydrogen and oxygen into electricity with approximately \(70\%\) efficiency.

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Dry cell pairs with the primary cell possessing a zinc container anode and carbon cathode giving about \(1.5\text{ V}\).
Mercury cell pairs with the system using zinc-mercury amalgam and maintaining a constant voltage of about \(1.35\text{ V}\).
Lead storage battery pairs with the secondary cell containing lead dioxide cathode and \(38\%\) sulphuric acid.
Fuel cell pairs with the device directly converting heat of combustion of gaseous fuels into electricity with about \(70\%\) efficiency.

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
The operational characteristics accurately represent the technological properties described in textbook Section 2.6 and Section 2.7.
Final Conceptual Answer: Dry cell pairs with IV, mercury cell pairs with I, lead storage battery pairs with II, and fuel cell pairs with III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q03 - Match external opposing potential with cell behavior

questiontext.text:
For a standard Daniell cell (\(E^\circ = 1.1\text{ V}\)) with \(1\text{ M}\) \(\text{Zn}^{2+}\) and \(1\text{ M}\) \(\text{Cu}^{2+}\) solutions, match the applied opposing external potential (\(E_{\text{ext}}\)) in List I with the observed cell behavior in List II:

List IList II
A. \(E_{\text{ext}} = 0\text{ V}\)I. Reaction stops completely; no current or electron flow occurs
B. \(E_{\text{ext}} < 1.1\text{ V}\)II. Cell functions as an electrolytic cell; zinc deposits on zinc rod and copper dissolves
C. \(E_{\text{ext}} = 1.1\text{ V}\)III. Spontaneous galvanic reaction proceeds at full standard potential; electrons flow from zinc to copper
D. \(E_{\text{ext}} > 1.1\text{ V}\)IV. Galvanic cell continues to discharge; electrons flow from zinc to copper but under reduced net driving voltage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Principles of Opposing Potential
The standard Daniell cell provides an electromotive force of \(1.1\text{ V}\). When an opposing external voltage \(E_{\text{ext}}\) is connected across the electrodes, the net cell behavior depends on the magnitude of \(E_{\text{ext}}\) relative to \(1.1\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Analysis of Each Condition
At \(E_{\text{ext}} = 0\text{ V}\), no opposing potential is present, so the cell operates spontaneously as a normal galvanic cell, driving electron flow from the zinc rod to the copper rod at full standard potential of \(1.1\text{ V}\).
When \(E_{\text{ext}} < 1.1\text{ V}\), the opposing voltage reduces the net electromotive force, but the cell continues to function galvanically with electrons flowing from zinc to copper and zinc dissolving at the anode.
When \(E_{\text{ext}} = 1.1\text{ V}\), the external counter-potential exactly balances the internal cell potential. No net chemical change occurs, and electrical current is zero.
When \(E_{\text{ext}} > 1.1\text{ V}\), the external voltage overcomes the cell potential and forces the reverse non-spontaneous reaction. The cell functions as an electrolytic cell, wherein electrons flow from copper to zinc, zinc deposits at the zinc electrode, and copper dissolves at the copper electrode.

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
An external potential of \(0\text{ V}\) corresponds to spontaneous galvanic reaction at full standard potential.
An external potential less than \(1.1\text{ V}\) corresponds to continued galvanic discharge under reduced net driving voltage.
An external potential equal to \(1.1\text{ V}\) corresponds to complete cessation of chemical reaction and zero current.
An external potential exceeding \(1.1\text{ V}\) corresponds to electrolytic cell operation with zinc deposition and copper dissolution.

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
The operational outcomes align with the principles illustrated in textbook opposing cell potential concepts.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with III, B pairs with IV, C pairs with I, and D pairs with II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q04 - Match electrode processes with electrochemical systems

questiontext.text:
Match the electrochemical system and electrode process in List I with the corresponding chemical reaction in List II:

List IList II
A. Cathode reaction in dry cellI. \(\text{O}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\)
B. Anode reaction in mercury cellII. \(\text{PbO}_2(\text{s}) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(\text{aq}) + 4\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4(\text{s}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\)
C. Cathode reaction during discharge of lead storage batteryIII. \(\text{Zn(Hg)} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{ZnO}(\text{s}) + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^-\)
D. Cathodic reaction during atmospheric rusting of ironIV. \(\text{MnO}_2 + \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{MnO(OH)} + \text{NH}_3\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Identification of Electrode Half-Reactions
Specific reduction and oxidation processes take place at designated electrode surfaces in batteries and corrosion cells.

Step 2: Reaction Breakdown for Each System
At the cathode of a dry cell, manganese dioxide is reduced in the presence of ammonium ions: \(\text{MnO}_2 + \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{MnO(OH)} + \text{NH}_3\), reducing manganese from \(+4\) to \(+3\).
At the anode of a mercury cell, zinc amalgam undergoes oxidation in the alkaline medium: \(\text{Zn(Hg)} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{ZnO}(\text{s}) + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^-\).
At the cathode of a lead storage battery during discharge, lead dioxide is reduced in acidic sulphate solution: \(\text{PbO}_2(\text{s}) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(\text{aq}) + 4\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4(\text{s}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\).
At the cathodic spot during the atmospheric rusting of iron, atmospheric oxygen dissolved in surface moisture is reduced by electrons arriving from anodic spots: \(\text{O}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\Defaultgrade.

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Cathode reaction in dry cell pairs with \(\text{MnO}_2 + \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{MnO(OH)} + \text{NH}_3\).
Anode reaction in mercury cell pairs with \(\text{Zn(Hg)} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{ZnO}(\text{s}) + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{e}^-\).
Cathode reaction in lead storage battery pairs with \(\text{PbO}_2(\text{s}) + \text{SO}_4^{2-}(\text{aq}) + 4\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4(\text{s}) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\).
Cathodic reaction during atmospheric rusting of iron pairs with \(\text{O}_2(\text{g}) + 4\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + 4\text{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})\).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
The electron transfers, stoichiometry, and oxidation states match the authoritative chemical equations in Sections 2.6.1, 2.6.2, and 2.8.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with IV, B pairs with III, C pairs with II, and D pairs with I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q05 - Match electrolytic systems with electrolysis products

questiontext.text:
Match the electrolyte being electrolysed using inert platinum electrodes in List I with the major electrode products in List II:

List IList II
A. Molten \(\text{NaCl}\)I. \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at cathode and \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}(\text{aq})\) at anode
B. Aqueous \(\text{NaCl}\)II. \(\text{Na}(\text{s})\) at cathode and \(\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\) at anode
C. Dilute \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\)III. \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at cathode and \(\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\) at anode
D. Concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\)IV. \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at cathode and \(\text{O}_2(\text{g})\) at anode

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Principles of Electrolysis and Competing Electrode Reactions
At the cathode, the cation or species with the higher reduction potential discharges first. At the anode, the anion or species with the lower oxidation potential discharges preferentially unless overpotential effects dictate otherwise.

Step 2: Analysis of Each Electrolyte
In molten \(\text{NaCl}\), only \(\text{Na}^+\) and \(\text{Cl}^-\) ions are present. \(\text{Na}^+\) is reduced to \(\text{Na}(\text{s})\) at the cathode, and \(\text{Cl}^-\) is oxidised to \(\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\) at the anode.
In aqueous \(\text{NaCl}\), reduction of water to \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) occurs at the cathode because its reduction potential is substantially higher than that of \(\text{Na}^+\) (\(-2.71\text{ V}\)). At the anode, although oxidation of water to \(\text{O}_2\) has a slightly lower standard potential (\(1.23\text{ V}\) versus \(1.36\text{ V}\) for chloride), the kinetic overpotential of oxygen makes chloride oxidation faster, producing \(\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\).
In dilute \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), \(\text{H}^+\) is reduced to \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at the cathode, and water is oxidised to \(\text{O}_2(\text{g})\) at the anode (\(E^\circ = 1.23\text{ V}\)).
In concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), the high concentration of sulphate ions favors oxidation to peroxodisulphate at the anode: \(2\text{SO}_4^{2-} \rightarrow \text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-} + 2\text{e}^-\) (\(E^\circ = 1.96\text{ V}\)), with \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) liberating at the cathode.

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Molten \(\text{NaCl}\) produces \(\text{Na}(\text{s})\) at cathode and \(\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\) at anode.
Aqueous \(\text{NaCl}\) produces \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at cathode and \(\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})\) at anode.
Dilute \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) produces \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at cathode and \(\text{O}_2(\text{g})\) at anode.
Concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) produces \(\text{H}_2(\text{g})\) at cathode and \(\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}(\text{aq})\) at anode.

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
Thermodynamic potentials and kinetic overpotentials corroborate each electrode assignment.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with II, B pairs with III, C pairs with IV, and D pairs with I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q06 - Match ionic species with limiting molar conductivities

questiontext.text:
Using the limiting molar ionic conductivities at \(298\text{ K}\) (\(\lambda^\circ\) in \(\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\): \(\text{Ca}^{2+} = 119.0\), \(\text{Mg}^{2+} = 106.0\), \(\text{Cl}^- = 76.3\), \(\text{SO}_4^{2-} = 160.0\), \(\text{Na}^+ = 50.1\), \(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- = 40.9\)), match the electrolyte in List I with its limiting molar conductivity \(\Lambda_m^\circ\) (in \(\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)) in List II:

List IList II
A. \(\text{CaCl}_2\)I. \(126.4\)
B. \(\text{MgSO}_4\)II. \(266.0\)
C. \(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}\)III. \(271.6\)
D. \(\text{NaCl}\)IV. \(91.0\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Principle (Kohlrausch Law)
Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions states that the limiting molar conductivity of an electrolyte equals the sum of the individual contributions of its constituent ions: \(\Lambda_m^\circ = \nu_+ \lambda_+^\circ + \nu_- \lambda_-^\circ\).

Step 2: Step-by-Step Numerical Additions
For \(\text{CaCl}_2\):
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CaCl}_2) = \lambda^\circ(\text{Ca}^{2+}) + 2\lambda^\circ(\text{Cl}^-) = 119.0 + 2(76.3) = 119.0 + 152.6 = 271.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
For \(\text{MgSO}_4\):
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{MgSO}_4) = \lambda^\circ(\text{Mg}^{2+}) + \lambda^\circ(\text{SO}_4^{2-}) = 106.0 + 160.0 = 266.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
For \(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}\):
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}) = \lambda^\circ(\text{Na}^+) + \lambda^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-) = 50.1 + 40.9 = 91.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
For \(\text{NaCl}\):
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl}) = \lambda^\circ(\text{Na}^+) + \lambda^\circ(\text{Cl}^-) = 50.1 + 76.3 = 126.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
\(\text{CaCl}_2\) yields \(271.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\text{MgSO}_4\) yields \(266.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}\) yields \(91.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\text{NaCl}\) yields \(126.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
Stoichiometric coefficients are appropriately applied for the divalent and univalent electrolytes.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with III, B pairs with II, C pairs with IV, and D pairs with I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q07 - Match redox couples with standard electrode potentials

questiontext.text:
Match the redox couples in List I with their standard reduction potentials \(E^\circ\) at \(298\text{ K}\) in List II:

List IList II
A. \(\text{F}_2(\text{g}) / \text{F}^-\)I. \(-0.76\text{ V}\)
B. \(\text{Cu}^{2+} / \text{Cu(s)}\)II. \(+2.87\text{ V}\)
C. \(\text{Zn}^{2+} / \text{Zn(s)}\)III. \(-3.05\text{ V}\)
D. \(\text{Li}^+ / \text{Li(s)}\)IV. \(+0.34\text{ V}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Concept of Electrochemical Series
The standard reduction potential measures the thermodynamic tendency of a chemical species to accept electrons relative to the standard hydrogen electrode, which is set to \(0.00\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Detailed Values from the Standard Reduction Table
Fluorine exhibits the highest standard electrode potential in the electrochemical table, with \(E^\circ(\text{F}_2 / \text{F}^-) = +2.87\text{ V}\), indicating that fluorine gas is the strongest oxidising agent.
The copper couple has a positive potential: \(E^\circ(\text{Cu}^{2+} / \text{Cu}) = +0.34\text{ V}\).
The zinc couple has a negative potential: \(E^\circ(\text{Zn}^{2+} / \text{Zn}) = -0.76\text{ V}\).
Lithium has the lowest standard potential: \(E^\circ(\text{Li}^+ / \text{Li}) = -3.05\text{ V}\), which establishes lithium metal as the most powerful reducing agent in aqueous solution.

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
\(\text{F}_2(\text{g}) / \text{F}^-\) corresponds to \(+2.87\text{ V}\).
\(\text{Cu}^{2+} / \text{Cu(s)}\) corresponds to \(+0.34\text{ V}\).
\(\text{Zn}^{2+} / \text{Zn(s)}\) corresponds to \(-0.76\text{ V}\).
\(\text{Li}^+ / \text{Li(s)}\) corresponds to \(-3.05\text{ V}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
The potential values match those tabulated in textbook standard reduction potential series at \(298\text{ K}\).
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with II, B pairs with IV, C pairs with I, and D pairs with III.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q08 - Match electrochemical conversions with charge required

questiontext.text:
Match the electrochemical conversion in List I with the theoretical quantity of electrical charge required in List II (using \(1\text{ F} \approx 96500\text{ C}\)):

List IList II
A. Reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) to \(\text{Al}\)I. \(1\text{ F}\) (\(96500\text{ C}\))
B. Oxidation of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) to \(\text{O}_2\)II. \(5\text{ F}\) (\(482500\text{ C}\))
C. Reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) to \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\)III. \(2\text{ F}\) (\(193000\text{ C}\))
D. Oxidation of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{FeO}\) to \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\)IV. \(3\text{ F}\) (\(289500\text{ C}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Principle (Faraday's Laws of Electrolysis)
The total charge required to carry out an electrochemical transformation is determined by the reaction stoichiometry: \(Q = n F\), where \(n\) is the number of moles of electrons transferred per mole of substance.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Stoichiometric Calculations
For the reduction of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) to \(\text{Al}\):
The cathode reaction is \(\text{Al}^{3+} + 3\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Al}\).
Reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) requires \(3\text{ mol}\) of electrons: \(Q = 3\text{ F} = 3 \times 96500\text{ C} = 289500\text{ C}\).
For the oxidation of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) to \(\text{O}_2\):
The balanced half-reaction is \(2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^-\).
Normalising for \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\): \(\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^-\).
Thus, \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) releases \(2\text{ mol}\) of electrons: \(Q = 2\text{ F} = 2 \times 96500\text{ C} = 193000\text{ C}\).
For the reduction of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) to \(\text{Mn}^{2+}\) in acidic solution:
The reaction is \(\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}\).
Manganese undergoes a change in oxidation state from \(+7\) to \(+2\), requiring \(5\text{ mol}\) of electrons: \(Q = 5\text{ F} = 5 \times 96500\text{ C} = 482500\text{ C}\).
For the oxidation of \(\text{FeO}\) to \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\):
In \(\text{FeO}\), iron has oxidation state \(+2\), while in \(\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\), iron has oxidation state \(+3\).
The half-reaction per mole of iron(II) is \(\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow \text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{e}^-\).
Therefore, \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{FeO}\) releases \(1\text{ mol}\) of electrons: \(Q = 1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C}\).

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) requires \(3\text{ F}\) (\(289500\text{ C}\)).
Oxidation of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) requires \(2\text{ F}\) (\(193000\text{ C}\)).
Reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{MnO}_4^-\) requires \(5\text{ F}\) (\(482500\text{ C}\)).
Oxidation of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{FeO}\) requires \(1\text{ F}\) (\(96500\text{ C}\)).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
The values correspond to textbook Exercises 2.12 and 2.14.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with IV, B pairs with III, C pairs with II, and D pairs with I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q09 - Match electrolytic relations with functional forms

questiontext.text:
Match the electrochemical formula or parameter in List I with its mathematically equivalent expression in List II:

List IList II
A. Cell constant (\(G^*\))I. \(\frac{c\Lambda_m^2}{\Lambda_m^\circ(\Lambda_m^\circ - \Lambda_m)}\)
B. Molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m\)) in terms of \(\kappa\) and molarity \(c\) (where \(\kappa\) is in \(\text{S cm}^{-1}\) and \(c\) in \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\))II. \(\Lambda_m^\circ - A c^{1/2}\)
C. Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation for strong electrolyteIII. \(\frac{\kappa \times 1000}{c}\)
D. Dissociation constant (\(K_a\)) of weak monobasic acid via Ostwald's dilution lawIV. \(R \cdot \kappa\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Electrochemical Equations
Electrolyte conductometry relies on specific mathematical formulations for geometric cell factors, unit conversions, empirical concentration dependencies, and weak electrolyte ionization equilibria.

Step 2: Detailed Algebraic Derivations
The cell constant is defined as \(G^* = \frac{l}{A}\). Because resistance is \(R = \frac{1}{\kappa}\frac{l}{A} = \frac{G^*}{\kappa}\), multiplying both sides by \(\kappa\) yields \(G^* = R \cdot \kappa\).
When conductivity \(\kappa\) is expressed in \(\text{S cm}^{-1}\) and concentration \(c\) in \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\), since \(1\text{ L} = 1000\text{ cm}^3\), the volume containing one mole of solute is \(V = \frac{1000}{c}\text{ cm}^3\text{ mol}^{-1}\). Hence, molar conductivity is given by \(\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{c}\) in \(\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
For a strong electrolyte, the Debye-Hückel-Onsager relation expresses the decrease of molar conductivity with square root of concentration as \(\Lambda_m = \Lambda_m^\circ - A c^{1/2}\).
For a weak monobasic acid, the degree of dissociation is given by \(\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ}\). Substituting this into Ostwald's dilution law \(K_a = \frac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}\) gives:
\(K_a = \frac{c (\Lambda_m / \Lambda_m^\circ)^2}{1 - (\Lambda_m / \Lambda_m^\circ)} = \frac{c \Lambda_m^2}{(\Lambda_m^\circ)^2 \left(\frac{\Lambda_m^\circ - \Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ}\right)} = \frac{c \Lambda_m^2}{\Lambda_m^\circ(\Lambda_m^\circ - \Lambda_m)}\).

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Cell constant pairs with \(R \cdot \kappa\).
Molar conductivity in \(\text{S cm}^{-1}\) and \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) pairs with \(\frac{\kappa \times 1000}{c}\).
Debye-Hückel-Onsager equation pairs with \(\Lambda_m^\circ - A c^{1/2}\).
Dissociation constant of weak monobasic acid pairs with \(\frac{c\Lambda_m^2}{\Lambda_m^\circ(\Lambda_m^\circ - \Lambda_m)}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
Every equation is rigorously confirmed against textbook Sections 2.4.1 and 2.4.2.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with IV, B pairs with III, C pairs with II, and D pairs with I.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MATCHING_MCQ_Q10 - Match thermodynamic and electrochemical equilibrium relationships

questiontext.text:
Match the electrochemical thermodynamic parameter or quantity in List I with its computed value or analytical expression at \(298\text{ K}\) in List II:

List IList II
A. Standard Gibbs energy change (\(\Delta_r G^\circ\)) for Daniell cell (\(E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = 1.1\text{ V}\), \(n = 2\), \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\))I. \(-nFE_{\text{cell}}\)
B. Equilibrium constant formulation (\(\log K_c\)) from standard cell potentialII. \(1.10\text{ V} - \frac{0.059}{2}\text{ V} = 1.0705\text{ V}\)
C. Gibbs energy change (\(\Delta_r G\)) of reaction at non-standard stateIII. \(-212.27\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)
D. Cell potential (\(E_{\text{cell}}\)) of Daniell cell when \(\frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} = 10\) at \(298\text{ K}\)IV. \(\frac{n E_{\text{cell}}^\circ}{0.059\text{ V}}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Relevant Thermodynamic and Electrochemical Equations
Electrical work performed reversibly relates to Gibbs free energy change via \(\Delta_r G = -nFE_{\text{cell}}\) and \(\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE_{\text{cell}}^\circ\). The equilibrium constant links to standard cell potential via \(E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = \frac{2.303RT}{nF}\log K_c = \frac{0.059\text{ V}}{n}\log K_c\) at \(298\text{ K}\), and concentration variations are given by the Nernst equation.

Step 2: Step-by-Step Numerical and Formulaic Evaluations
For the standard Daniell cell reaction \(\text{Zn(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + \text{Cu(s)}\):
Here \(n = 2\), \(E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = 1.1\text{ V}\), and \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\).
\(\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE_{\text{cell}}^\circ = -2 \times 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 1.1\text{ V} = -212271.4\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -212.27\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).
At equilibrium (\(E_{\text{cell}} = 0\)), \(E_{\text{cell}}^\circ = \frac{0.059\text{ V}}{n}\log K_c\).
Rearranging gives \(\log K_c = \frac{n E_{\text{cell}}^\circ}{0.059\text{ V}}\).
At non-standard conditions, the Gibbs free energy change is directly given by \(\Delta_r G = -nFE_{\text{cell}}\).
Applying the Nernst equation to the Daniell cell at \(298\text{ K}\):
\(E_{\text{cell}} = E_{\text{cell}}^\circ - \frac{0.059\text{ V}}{2}\log \frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]}\).
Substituting the concentration ratio \(\frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} = 10\):
Since \(\log(10) = 1\), \(E_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V} - \frac{0.059}{2}\text{ V} = 1.10\text{ V} - 0.0295\text{ V} = 1.0705\text{ V}\).

Step 3: Pairwise Matching Evaluation
Standard Gibbs energy change for the Daniell cell corresponds to \(-212.27\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).
Equilibrium constant expression corresponds to \(\frac{n E_{\text{cell}}^\circ}{0.059\text{ V}}\).
Gibbs energy change of reaction corresponds to \(-nFE_{\text{cell}}\).
Cell potential of Daniell cell when ion concentration ratio is \(10\) corresponds to \(1.10\text{ V} - \frac{0.059}{2}\text{ V} = 1.0705\text{ V}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Conceptual Answer
All derived values agree with the calculations presented in textbook Examples 2.1, 2.3 and Section 2.3.2.
Final Conceptual Answer: A pairs with III, B pairs with IV, C pairs with I, and D pairs with II.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q01 - Standard electromotive force calculation for Daniell cell

questiontext.text:
Given the standard reduction potentials for the half-cells at \(298\text{ K}\):

\[E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = +0.34\text{ V}\]

\[E^\circ_{\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}} = -0.76\text{ V}\]

What is the standard cell potential (\(E^\circ_{\text{cell}}\)) of the Daniell cell represented as \(\text{Zn(s)} \mid \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \parallel \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq)} \mid \text{Cu(s)}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Standard reduction potential of cathode (right electrode, copper): \(E^\circ_{\text{right}} = +0.34\text{ V}\).
Standard reduction potential of anode (left electrode, zinc): \(E^\circ_{\text{left}} = -0.76\text{ V}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
By IUPAC convention, standard cell potential is computed as the standard reduction potential of the cathode minus the standard reduction potential of the anode.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{right}} - E^\circ_{\text{left}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.34\text{ V} - (-0.76\text{ V}) = 0.34\text{ V} + 0.76\text{ V} = +1.10\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The cell potential is positive, corresponding to a spontaneous reaction under standard conditions with a value of \(+1.10\text{ V}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(+1.10\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Conductivity cell constant determination using potassium chloride

questiontext.text: The resistance of a conductivity cell containing \(0.001\text{ M KCl}\) solution at \(298\text{ K}\) is \(1500\ \Omega\). If the conductivity of \(0.001\text{ M KCl}\) solution at \(298\text{ K}\) is \(0.146 \times 10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1}\), what is the cell constant of the conductivity cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Resistance of the cell: \(R = 1500\ \Omega\).
Conductivity of the solution: \(\kappa = 0.146 \times 10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The cell constant \(G^*\) depends strictly on the geometry of the electrodes (\(l/A\)) and is related directly to resistance and conductivity.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[G^* = \frac{l}{A} = R \times \kappa\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[G^* = 1500\ \Omega \times 0.146 \times 10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1} = 0.219\text{ cm}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The product has units of \(\Omega \times \Omega^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1} = \text{cm}^{-1}\), yielding \(0.219\text{ cm}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.219\text{ cm}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q03 - Molar conductivity calculation of potassium chloride electrolyte

questiontext.text: The conductivity of a \(0.20\text{ M}\) solution of \(\text{KCl}\) at \(298\text{ K}\) is \(0.0248\text{ S cm}^{-1}\). What is its molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m\)) in \(\text{S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Molar concentration: \(c = 0.20\text{ M} = 0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Conductivity: \(\kappa = 0.0248\text{ S cm}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
Convert concentration from \(\text{mol L}^{-1}\) to \(\text{mol cm}^{-3}\) using \(1\text{ L} = 1000\text{ cm}^3\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa \times 1000}{c}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\Lambda_m = \frac{0.0248\text{ S cm}^{-1} \times 1000\text{ cm}^3\text{ L}^{-1}}{0.20\text{ mol L}^{-1}} = \frac{24.8}{0.20} = 124\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The molar conductivity evaluates to \(124\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(124\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q04 - Electrical charge required for aluminium ion reduction

questiontext.text: How much electrical charge in coulombs is required for the complete electrochemical reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\) ions to metallic aluminium? (Take \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Amount of substance: \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Al}^{3+}\).
Faraday constant: \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Electrode Reaction and Stoichiometry
The reduction half-reaction at the cathode is: \[\text{Al}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Al(s)}\] Reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of trivalent aluminium ions requires \(3\text{ moles}\) of electrons (\(3\text{ F}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[Q = n \times F\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[Q = 3 \times 96487\text{ C} = 289461\text{ C} \approx 2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Three moles of electrons correspond to approximately \(2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(289461\text{ C}\) (or \(2.89 \times 10^5\text{ C}\))

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q05 - Cell electromotive force computation under nonstandard concentration conditions

questiontext.text: A Daniell cell operates at \(298\text{ K}\) with \([\text{Zn}^{2+}] = 0.1\text{ M}\) and \([\text{Cu}^{2+}] = 1.0\text{ M}\). Given that \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V}\) and \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\), what is the electromotive force (\(E_{\text{cell}}\)) of the cell?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Standard cell potential: \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V}\).
Concentrations: \([\text{Zn}^{2+}] = 0.1\text{ M}\), \([\text{Cu}^{2+}] = 1.0\text{ M}\).
Electrons transferred: \(n = 2\).
Constant factor: \(0.059\text{ V}\) at \(298\text{ K}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
Apply the Nernst equation for the Daniell cell reaction: \[\text{Zn(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + \text{Cu(s)}\]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.059}{n} \log \frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Evaluate the concentration ratio: \[\frac{[\text{Zn}^{2+}]}{[\text{Cu}^{2+}]} = \frac{0.1}{1.0} = 10^{-1}\] Compute the logarithmic term: \[\log(10^{-1}) = -1\] Substitute into the formula: \[E_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V} - \frac{0.059}{2}(-1) = 1.10\text{ V} + 0.0295\text{ V} = 1.1295\text{ V} \approx 1.13\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Because reactant concentration exceeds product concentration, \(E_{\text{cell}} > E^\circ_{\text{cell}}\), yielding \(1.13\text{ V}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(1.13\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q06 - Hydrogen electrode potential computation at specified solution acidity

questiontext.text: Calculate the potential of a hydrogen electrode at \(298\text{ K}\) dipping in an aqueous solution of \(\text{pH} = 4\) under a hydrogen gas pressure of \(1\text{ bar}\). (Take \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\text{pH} = 4\).
Gas pressure: \(p_{\text{H}_2} = 1\text{ bar}\).
Temperature: \(T = 298\text{ K}\).
Electrode reaction: \(\text{H}^{+}(\text{aq}) + \mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2(\text{g})\).
Standard potential: \(E^\circ_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2} = 0.00\text{ V}\).
Number of electrons: \(n = 1\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
From the definition of pH, \([\text{H}^{+}] = 10^{-\text{pH}} = 10^{-4}\text{ M}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[E_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2} = E^\circ_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2} - \frac{0.059}{1} \log \frac{1}{[\text{H}^{+}]} = -0.059 \times \text{pH}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[E_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2} = -0.059 \times 4 = -0.236\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
At \([\text{H}^{+}] = 10^{-4}\text{ M}\) (lower than standard \(1\text{ M}\)), the reduction potential is negative, equal to \(-0.236\text{ V}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(-0.236\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q07 - Standard Gibbs free energy evaluation for zinc copper cell

questiontext.text: For the galvanic cell reaction \(\text{Zn(s)} + \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Zn}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + \text{Cu(s)}\), the standard cell potential is \(1.10\text{ V}\). What is the standard Gibbs energy change (\(\Delta_r G^\circ\)) of this reaction? (Take \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Standard cell potential: \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 1.10\text{ V}\).
Moles of electrons transferred: \(n = 2\).
Faraday constant: \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
The standard Gibbs energy change is related to the standard cell electromotive force by the thermodynamic relation for reversible electrochemical work.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\Delta_r G^\circ = -2 \times 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 1.10\text{ V} = -212271.4\text{ J mol}^{-1} \approx -212.27\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
A spontaneous reaction with positive \(E^\circ\) corresponds to a negative standard Gibbs energy of \(-212.27\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(-212.27\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q08 - Equilibrium constant computation for copper silver displacement reaction

questiontext.text:
The standard potential of the cell corresponding to the reaction:

\[\text{Cu(s)} + 2\text{Ag}^{+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + 2\text{Ag(s)}\]

is \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.46\text{ V}\) at \(298\text{ K}\). What is the equilibrium constant (\(K_c\)) of this reaction? (Take \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reaction: \(\text{Cu(s)} + 2\text{Ag}^{+}(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons \text{Cu}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + 2\text{Ag(s)}\).
Standard cell potential: \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.46\text{ V}\).
Number of electrons: \(n = 2\).
Factor: \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\) at \(298\text{ K}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
At dynamic equilibrium, the cell potential drops to zero (\(E_{\text{cell}} = 0\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = \frac{0.059}{n} \log K_c \implies \log K_c = \frac{n E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.059}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\log K_c = \frac{2 \times 0.46\text{ V}}{0.059\text{ V}} = \frac{0.92}{0.059} \approx 15.6\] Taking antilogarithm: \[K_c = 10^{15.6} = 10^{0.6} \times 10^{15} \approx 3.92 \times 10^{15}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
A standard potential of \(+0.46\text{ V}\) indicates an equilibrium constant of approximately \(3.92 \times 10^{15}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(3.92 \times 10^{15}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q09 - Resistivity and conductivity determination for cylindrical solution column

questiontext.text: A cylindrical column of an electrolytic solution has a diameter of \(1.0\text{ cm}\) and a length of \(50\text{ cm}\). Its electrical resistance is measured to be \(5.55 \times 10^3\ \Omega\). What are the resistivity (\(\rho\)) and conductivity (\(\kappa\)) of the solution in \(\text{cm}\)-based units?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Diameter: \(d = 1.0\text{ cm} \implies \text{radius } r = 0.5\text{ cm}\).
Length: \(l = 50\text{ cm}\).
Resistance: \(R = 5.55 \times 10^3\ \Omega\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
The column has uniform circular cross section. Cross-sectional area is \(A = \pi r^2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[A = 3.14 \times (0.5\text{ cm})^2 = 0.785\text{ cm}^2\] \[\rho = \frac{R A}{l}\] \[\kappa = \frac{1}{\rho}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate resistivity: \[\rho = \frac{5.55 \times 10^3\ \Omega \times 0.785\text{ cm}^2}{50\text{ cm}} = 87.135\ \Omega\text{ cm}\] Calculate conductivity: \[\kappa = \frac{1}{87.135\ \Omega\text{ cm}} \approx 0.01148\text{ S cm}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Resistivity is \(87.14\ \Omega\text{ cm}\) and conductivity is \(0.01148\text{ S cm}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(\rho = 87.14\ \Omega\text{ cm}\) and \(\kappa = 0.01148\text{ S cm}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q10 - Limiting molar conductivity calculation of calcium chloride salt

questiontext.text:
Given the limiting molar ionic conductivities at \(298\text{ K}\):

\[\lambda^\circ(\text{Ca}^{2+}) = 119.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\]

\[\lambda^\circ(\text{Cl}^-) = 76.3\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\]

What is the limiting molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m^\circ\)) of calcium chloride (\(\text{CaCl}_2\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\lambda^\circ(\text{Ca}^{2+}) = 119.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\lambda^\circ(\text{Cl}^-) = 76.3\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Principles and Stoichiometry
\(\text{CaCl}_2\) dissociates completely at infinite dilution according to: \[\text{CaCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{Ca}^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^-\] Stoichiometric coefficients are \(\nu_+ = 1\) and \(\nu_- = 2\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
By Kohlrausch's law of independent migration of ions: \[\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CaCl}_2) = \nu_+ \lambda^\circ(\text{Ca}^{2+}) + \nu_- \lambda^\circ(\text{Cl}^-) = \lambda^\circ(\text{Ca}^{2+}) + 2\lambda^\circ(\text{Cl}^-)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CaCl}_2) = 119.0 + 2(76.3) = 119.0 + 152.6 = 271.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Sum of individual ion conductivities gives \(271.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(271.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q11 - Limiting molar conductivity determination for weak acetic acid

questiontext.text: The limiting molar conductivities (\(\Lambda_m^\circ\)) for \(\text{NaCl}\), \(\text{HCl}\), and \(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}\) at \(298\text{ K}\) are \(126.4\), \(425.9\), and \(91.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\), respectively. What is the value of \(\Lambda_m^\circ\) for acetic acid (\(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl}) = 425.9\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}) = 91.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
\(\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl}) = 126.4\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Principles and Algebraic Combination
By Kohlrausch's law: \[\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = \lambda^\circ(\text{H}^+) + \lambda^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-)\] This can be expressed as: \[\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{HCl}) + \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}) - \Lambda_m^\circ(\text{NaCl})\]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
\[\Lambda_m^\circ(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = 425.9 + 91.0 - 126.4 = 516.9 - 126.4 = 390.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid is \(390.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(390.5\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q12 - Electricity required in Faradays for aluminium metal production

questiontext.text: How much electricity in terms of Faraday (\(F\)) is required to produce \(40.0\text{ g}\) of aluminium metal from molten \(\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3\)? (Molar mass of \(\text{Al} = 27.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mass of aluminium: \(m = 40.0\text{ g}\).
Molar mass of aluminium: \(M = 27.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}\).
Electrode reaction: \(\text{Al}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Al(s)}\).

Step 2: Principles and Stoichiometry
Deposition of \(1\text{ mol}\) (\(27.0\text{ g}\)) of aluminium requires \(3\text{ moles}\) of electrons, which equals \(3\text{ F}\) of electricity.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[n_{\text{Al}} = \frac{m}{M}\] \[Q (\text{in } F) = n_{\text{Al}} \times 3\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[n_{\text{Al}} = \frac{40.0\text{ g}}{27.0\text{ g mol}^{-1}} \approx 1.4815\text{ mol}\] \[Q = 1.4815 \times 3\text{ F} \approx 4.44\text{ F}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The electricity required is \(4.44\text{ F}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(4.44\text{ F}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q13 - Number of electrons flowing through wire during electrolysis

questiontext.text: If a steady electric current of \(0.5\text{ A}\) flows through a metallic wire for \(2\text{ hours}\), how many electrons flow through the wire? (Take charge on an electron as \(1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Current: \(I = 0.5\text{ A}\).
Time: \(t = 2\text{ hours} = 2 \times 3600\text{ s} = 7200\text{ s}\).
Elementary charge: \(e = 1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
Electric charge is the product of current and time: \(Q = I \times t\). Total number of electrons is \(N = Q / e\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[Q = I t\] \[N = \frac{Q}{e}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate total charge: \[Q = 0.5\text{ A} \times 7200\text{ s} = 3600\text{ C}\] Calculate number of electrons: \[N = \frac{3600\text{ C}}{1.602 \times 10^{-19}\text{ C}} \approx 2.247 \times 10^{22} \approx 2.25 \times 10^{22}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
A charge of \(3600\text{ C}\) corresponds to \(2.25 \times 10^{22}\) electrons.

Final Conceptual Answer: \(2.25 \times 10^{22}\) electrons

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q14 - Quantity of electricity in coulombs for dichromate reduction

questiontext.text:
Consider the acidic reduction reaction of dichromate ion:

\[\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}(\text{aq}) + 14\text{H}^{+}(\text{aq}) + 6\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}(l)\]

What is the quantity of electricity in coulombs needed to reduce \(1\text{ mol}\) of \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\)? (Take \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\))

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reaction: \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 14\text{H}^{+} + 6\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 7\text{H}_2\text{O}\).
Amount of \(\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\): \(1\text{ mol}\).
Faraday constant: \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Principles and Stoichiometry
From the balanced half-reaction, reduction of \(1\text{ mol}\) of dichromate requires \(6\text{ moles}\) of electrons (\(6\text{ F}\)).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[Q = n \times F = 6 \times F\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
\[Q = 6 \times 96487\text{ C} = 578922\text{ C} \approx 5.79 \times 10^5\text{ C}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The quantity of electricity is \(5.79 \times 10^5\text{ C}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(5.79 \times 10^5\text{ C}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q15 - Nernst equation cell potential calculation for magnesium silver system

questiontext.text:
A galvanic cell operates according to the reaction:

\[\text{Mg(s)} + 2\text{Ag}^{+}(0.0001\text{ M}) \rightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+}(0.130\text{ M}) + 2\text{Ag(s)}\]

Given that \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 3.17\text{ V}\) and \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\) at \(298\text{ K}\), what is the cell electromotive force (\(E_{\text{cell}}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Standard cell potential: \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 3.17\text{ V}\).
Concentrations: \([\text{Mg}^{2+}] = 0.130\text{ M}\), \([\text{Ag}^{+}] = 0.0001\text{ M} = 10^{-4}\text{ M}\).
Moles of electrons: \(n = 2\).
Factor: \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\) at \(298\text{ K}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
Solid magnesium and solid silver have constant unit activities.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.059}{n} \log \frac{[\text{Mg}^{2+}]}{[\text{Ag}^{+}]^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate reaction quotient: \[Q = \frac{0.130}{(10^{-4})^2} = \frac{0.130}{10^{-8}} = 1.30 \times 10^7\] Evaluate logarithm: \[\log(1.30 \times 10^7) = \log 1.30 + 7 \approx 0.1139 + 7 = 7.1139\] Compute reduction term: \[\frac{0.059}{2} \times 7.1139 \approx 0.0295 \times 7.1139 \approx 0.21\text{ V}\] Calculate cell potential: \[E_{\text{cell}} = 3.17\text{ V} - 0.21\text{ V} = 2.96\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The cell potential is \(2.96\text{ V}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(2.96\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q16 - Nernst equation potential calculation for tin hydrogen gas cell

questiontext.text:
For the electrochemical cell at \(298\text{ K}\):

\[\text{Sn(s)} \mid \text{Sn}^{2+}(0.050\text{ M}) \parallel \text{H}^{+}(0.020\text{ M}) \mid \text{H}_2(\text{g}, 1\text{ bar}) \mid \text{Pt(s)}\]

Given standard potentials \(E^\circ_{\text{Sn}^{2+}/\text{Sn}} = -0.14\text{ V}\), \(E^\circ_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2} = 0.00\text{ V}\), and \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\), what is the cell potential (\(E_{\text{cell}}\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Anode reaction: \(\text{Sn(s)} \rightarrow \text{Sn}^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\mathrm{e}^-\), \(E^\circ = -0.14\text{ V}\).
Cathode reaction: \(2\text{H}^{+}(\text{aq}) + 2\mathrm{e}^- \rightarrow \text{H}_2(\text{g})\), \(E^\circ = 0.00\text{ V}\).
Overall reaction: \(\text{Sn(s)} + 2\text{H}^{+}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{Sn}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + \text{H}_2(\text{g})\).
Number of electrons: \(n = 2\).
Concentrations: \([\text{Sn}^{2+}] = 0.050\text{ M}\), \([\text{H}^{+}] = 0.020\text{ M}\), \(p_{\text{H}_2} = 1\text{ bar}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Model
\[E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cathode}} - E^\circ_{\text{anode}} = 0.00 - (-0.14) = +0.14\text{ V}\]

Step 3: Relevant Formulae
\[E_{\text{cell}} = E^\circ_{\text{cell}} - \frac{0.059}{2} \log \frac{[\text{Sn}^{2+}] p_{\text{H}_2}}{[\text{H}^{+}]^2}\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute reaction quotient: \[Q = \frac{0.050 \times 1}{(0.020)^2} = \frac{0.050}{0.00040} = 125\] Compute logarithm: \[\log 125 = \log(5^3) = 3 \log 5 = 3 \times 0.69897 = 2.0969\] Compute deduction term: \[\frac{0.059}{2} \times 2.0969 = 0.0295 \times 2.0969 \approx 0.0619\text{ V} \approx 0.062\text{ V}\] Calculate cell potential: \[E_{\text{cell}} = 0.14\text{ V} - 0.062\text{ V} = 0.078\text{ V}\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The cell potential is \(0.078\text{ V}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(0.078\text{ V}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q17 - Standard Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant for ferric iodide system

questiontext.text:
For the cell in which the reaction occurs at \(298\text{ K}\):

\[2\text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{I}^{-}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + \text{I}_2(\text{s})\]

The standard cell potential is \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.236\text{ V}\). Taking \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\) and \(\frac{2.303RT}{F} = 0.059\text{ V}\), what are the standard Gibbs energy change (\(\Delta_r G^\circ\)) and the equilibrium constant (\(K_c\)) of the reaction?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Reaction: \(2\text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{I}^{-}(\text{aq}) \rightarrow 2\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{aq)} + \text{I}_2(\text{s})\).
Standard cell potential: \(E^\circ_{\text{cell}} = 0.236\text{ V}\).
Moles of electrons: \(n = 2\).
Faraday constant: \(F = 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
\[\Delta_r G^\circ = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}}\] \[\log K_c = \frac{n E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.059}\]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate \(\Delta_r G^\circ\): \[\Delta_r G^\circ = -2 \times 96487\text{ C mol}^{-1} \times 0.236\text{ V} = -45541.86\text{ J mol}^{-1} \approx -45.54\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\] Calculate \(\log K_c\): \[\log K_c = \frac{2 \times 0.236}{0.059} = \frac{0.472}{0.059} = 8.0\] Taking antilogarithm: \[K_c = 10^{8.0} \text{ (or } 9.62 \times 10^7 \text{ using exact } 0.05916\text{ V)}\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
\(\Delta_r G^\circ = -45.54\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) and \(K_c = 9.62 \times 10^7\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(\Delta_r G^\circ = -45.54\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}\) and \(K_c = 9.62 \times 10^7\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q18 - Degree of dissociation and dissociation constant for methanoic acid

questiontext.text: The molar conductivity of \(0.025\text{ mol L}^{-1}\) methanoic acid (\(\text{HCOOH}\)) is \(46.1\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\). Given limiting ionic conductivities \(\lambda^\circ(\text{H}^+) = 349.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\) and \(\lambda^\circ(\text{HCOO}^-) = 54.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\), what are its degree of dissociation (\(\alpha\)) and dissociation constant (\(K_a\))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Concentration: \(c = 0.025\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).
Molar conductivity: \(\Lambda_m = 46.1\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).
Limiting conductivities: \(\lambda^\circ(\text{H}^+) = 349.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\), \(\lambda^\circ(\text{HCOO}^-) = 54.6\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
\[\Lambda_m^\circ = \lambda^\circ(\text{H}^+) + \lambda^\circ(\text{HCOO}^-)\] \[\alpha = \frac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ}\] \[K_a = \frac{c \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}\]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate limiting molar conductivity: \[\Lambda_m^\circ = 349.6 + 54.6 = 404.2\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\] Calculate degree of dissociation: \[\alpha = \frac{46.1}{404.2} \approx 0.11405 \approx 0.114\] Calculate dissociation constant: \[K_a = \frac{0.025 \times (0.114)^2}{1 - 0.114} = \frac{0.025 \times 0.012996}{0.886} \approx 3.67 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
\(\alpha = 0.114\) and \(K_a = 3.67 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(\alpha = 0.114\) and \(K_a = 3.67 \times 10^{-4}\text{ mol L}^{-1}\)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ELECTROCHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q19 - Sequential cell constant conductivity and molar conductivity computation

questiontext.text: The resistance of a conductivity cell filled with \(0.1\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{ KCl}\) solution is \(100\ \Omega\). When the same cell is filled with \(0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{ KCl}\) solution, the resistance is \(520\ \Omega\). Given that the conductivity of \(0.1\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{ KCl}\) solution is \(1.29\text{ S m}^{-1}\), what are the conductivity (\(\kappa\)) and molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m\)) of the \(0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1}\text{ KCl}\) solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
First solution (\(0.1\text{ M KCl}\)): \(R_1 = 100\ \Omega\), \(\kappa_1 = 1.29\text{ S m}^{-1}\).
Second solution (\(0.02\text{ M KCl}\)): \(R_2 = 520\ \Omega\), \(c_2 = 0.02\text{ mol L}^{-1} = 20\text{ mol m}^{-3}\).

Step 2: Relevant Formulae
\[G^* = R_1 \times \kappa_1\] \[\kappa_2 = \frac{G^*}{R_2}\] \[\Lambda_m = \frac{\kappa_2}{c_2}\]

Step 3: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate cell constant: \[G^* = 100\ \Omega \times 1.29\text{ S m}^{-1} = 129\text{ m}^{-1} = 1.29\text{ cm}^{-1}\] Calculate conductivity of \(0.02\text{ M KCl}\): \[\kappa_2 = \frac{129\text{ m}^{-1}}{520\ \Omega} \approx 0.248\text{ S m}^{-1} = 0.248 \times 10^{-2}\text{ S cm}^{-1}\] Calculate molar conductivity: \[\Lambda_m = \frac{0.248\text{ S m}^{-1}}{20\text{ mol m}^{-3}} = 124 \times 10^{-4}\text{ S m}^2\text{ mol}^{-1} = 124\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\]

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
\(\kappa = 0.248\text{ S m}^{-1}\) and \(\Lambda_m = 124\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\).

Final Conceptual Answer: \(\kappa = 0.248\text{ S m}^{-1}\) and \(\Lambda_m = 124\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}\)
